## Project and Mission

**BioReport** is a modular, configurable bioinformatics report engine built with Python and Quarto, and a core delivery component of the **CygnusX BioOps** research software ecosystem.

Tables, figures and logs scattered across analysis tools make scientific review and delivery costly. BioReport connects existing computational outputs to structured, interactive, interpretable and verifiable research reports.

::: {.mission-grid}
::: {.mission-card}
<div class="mission-badge">ECOSYSTEM VISION</div>
<div class="mission-en">From Research Questions to Reproducible Scientific Evidence.</div>
<div class="mission-cn">Organize controlled computational experiments around research questions to produce verifiable, traceable and reproducible evidence.</div>
:::
::: {.mission-card}
<div class="mission-badge">CORE MISSION</div>
<div class="mission-en">From Analysis Results to Verifiable Research Reports.</div>
<div class="mission-cn">Make research results clear to communicate, effective to review and useful to the continuing accumulation of scientific knowledge.</div>
:::
:::

## Capabilities and Technical Architecture

BioReport separates an **omics-independent rendering engine** from **domain analysis modules**, turning repetitive manual report preparation into a configurable, maintainable and reusable engineering process.

::: {.callout-strip}
Define once, compose as needed. Separate results from presentation and reuse reporting components.
:::

### Core Features

::: {.feature-grid}

::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-head"><span class="feature-title">Configuration-driven</span><span class="feature-tag">Declarative configuration</span></div>
<div class="feature-desc">Manage report structure, modules, parameters and output formats through JSON / YAML configuration.</div>
:::

::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-head"><span class="feature-title">Modular Reporting</span><span class="feature-tag">Domain modules</span></div>
<div class="feature-desc">Combine project summaries, samples, quality control, differential analysis and enrichment as needed. RNA-seq is supported today, with an extensible foundation for other omics.</div>
:::

::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-head"><span class="feature-title">Interactive Visualization</span><span class="feature-tag">Explore and review</span></div>
<div class="feature-desc">Explore interactive charts and searchable high-dimensional tables, with HTML delivery and dedicated PDF templates for print and archiving.</div>
:::

::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-head"><span class="feature-title">AI-assisted Interpretation</span><span class="feature-tag">Optional scientific support</span></div>
<div class="feature-desc">Optionally use language models to interpret differential expression and enriched pathways. Researchers must review generated interpretations against the underlying evidence.</div>
:::

:::

### Report Generation Architecture

The engine reads existing analysis results, selects chapters and binds input files and display parameters from JSON / YAML configuration, then composes Quarto documents for interactive HTML or print-ready PDF. Optional AI interpretations are prepared for insertion into the relevant result sections.

::: {.arch-figure}
```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  Config["JSON / YAML configuration<br/>JSON Schema validation"] --> Control["CLI: validation and orchestration"]
  RNA["RNA-seq modules: omics/rna"] --> Compose["Module registry, selection and composition"]
  Custom["Custom QMD modules"] --> Compose
  Theme["Jinja2 templates and shared theme"] --> Stage["Temporary Quarto project<br/>QMD, configuration and assets"]
  Control --> Compose --> Stage
  Data["Existing analysis results and project metadata"] --> Analysis["Read results, summarize and plot"]
  Stage --> Execute["Quarto / Jupyter: execute selected modules"]
  Data --> Execute
  Execute --> Analysis
  Analysis --> HTMLView["HTML: Plotly / ITables"] --> HTML["Single-file / multi-page HTML"]
  Analysis --> PDFView["PDF figures: static SVG and Typst"]
  PDFView --> FirstPDF["First PDF render<br/>Figures and block manifest"]
  FirstPDF --> Evidence["Structured evidence and rendered images"]
  Control -.-> AIPre["AI interpretation: HTML / non-visual path"]
  Data -.-> AIPre
  AIPre -.-> Markdown["Per-result Markdown cards"]
  Markdown -.-> Stage
  Evidence -.-> AIPost["AI visual interpretation: two-pass PDF path"]
  AIPost -.-> Markdown
  Markdown -.-> SecondPDF["Second PDF render<br/>Insert result interpretations"]
  SecondPDF --> PDF["PDF report and layout validation"]
  Control --> Records["Run logs, configuration backup and manifests"]
  Evidence -.-> Records
  AIPost -.-> Records
  classDef plain fill:#ffffff,stroke:#94a3b8,color:#334155;
  classDef blue fill:#eff6ff,stroke:#3b82f6,color:#173258;
  classDef green fill:#f0fdf4,stroke:#22a06b,color:#14532d;
  classDef optional fill:#faf5ff,stroke:#a78bfa,color:#553285;
  class Config,Data,RNA,Custom,Theme,HTMLView,PDFView plain;
  class Control,Compose,Stage,Execute,Analysis blue;
  class HTML,PDF,Records,FirstPDF,SecondPDF green;
  class AIPre,AIPost,Markdown,Evidence optional;
```
:::
::: {.arch-caption}
Configuration combines domain modules and shared templates. Quarto executes the selected modules to read results and create figures for interactive HTML or print PDF. AI interpretation is optional; Docker provides a containerized generation environment.
:::

Runtime: local Python + Quarto, or Docker. Read delivered reports in a browser or PDF reader.

### Technology by Responsibility

::: {.tech-roles}

::: {.tech-role}
<div class="tech-role-head"><span class="tech-role-name">Configuration and orchestration</span><span class="tech-role-tools">Python · JSON / YAML · JSON Schema</span></div>
<div class="tech-role-desc">Load and validate configuration, resolve paths, select modules, check inputs and orchestrate report generation.</div>
:::

::: {.tech-role}
<div class="tech-role-head"><span class="tech-role-name">Modules and content composition</span><span class="tech-role-tools">Registry · QMD · Module composer · Jinja2</span></div>
<div class="tech-role-desc">Register domain modules and input requirements, compose chapters, pass parameters and generate Quarto configuration and templates.</div>
:::

::: {.tech-role}
<div class="tech-role-head"><span class="tech-role-name">Data processing and interactive presentation</span><span class="tech-role-tools">pandas / NumPy · Plotly · ITables</span></div>
<div class="tech-role-desc">Read existing QC, expression, differential analysis and enrichment results for summaries, figures and searchable tables.</div>
:::

::: {.tech-role}
<div class="tech-role-head"><span class="tech-role-name">Rendering and delivery</span><span class="tech-role-tools">Quarto · Jupyter · Static figures · Typst</span></div>
<div class="tech-role-desc">HTML supports interactive review. PDF uses dedicated chapters, pagination-aware static figures and Typst. Both formats share analysis functions while using their own content templates.</div>
:::

::: {.tech-role}
<div class="tech-role-head"><span class="tech-role-name">Optional AI interpretation</span><span class="tech-role-tools">Language models · Markdown</span></div>
<div class="tech-role-desc">When selected and enabled, AI modules summarize specified differential and enrichment results as Markdown before rendering. Researchers review model-generated content.</div>
:::

::: {.tech-role}
<div class="tech-role-head"><span class="tech-role-name">Runtime environment</span><span class="tech-role-tools">Local Python / Quarto · Docker</span></div>
<div class="tech-role-desc">Render templates, execute code and build documents locally or in containers. Containers reduce environment differences without guaranteeing byte-for-byte cross-platform reproduction.</div>
:::

:::

::: {.callout-strip}
Configuration defines structure; modules carry content. Reuse analysis functions and adapt delivery to the format.
:::

## CygnusX Research Ecosystem

BioReport runs independently and works with the wider **CygnusX BioOps** ecosystem to connect scientific questions with trustworthy computational results.

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| **[GeoMuse](https://github.com/xsx123123/GeoMuse)** | Public omics data and literature discovery; research evidence retrieval and organization |
| **[Polariseq](https://github.com/xsx123123/polariseq)** | Efficient acquisition, download and transfer of public sequencing data |
| **[FlowFrame](https://github.com/xsx123123/FlowFrame)** | Versioned, standardized bioinformatics workflows |
| **[BioReport](https://github.com/xsx123123/bioreport)** | Analysis result organization, interactive visualization and standardized report delivery |
| **[CygnusX BioOps](https://github.com/xsx123123/OmicHub_BioOps)** | Governed research agents, workflow orchestration, trustworthy computation and evidence tracking |

Four engineering principles guide the ecosystem:

::: {.pill-row}

::: {.pill-badge}
<span class="pill-dot"></span><span class="pill-en">Research Agents</span>
:::

::: {.pill-badge}
<span class="pill-dot"></span><span class="pill-en">Reproducible Workflows</span>
:::

::: {.pill-badge}
<span class="pill-dot"></span><span class="pill-en">Governed Execution</span>
:::

::: {.pill-badge}
<span class="pill-dot"></span><span class="pill-en">Verifiable Evidence</span>
:::

:::
